mainTopic: Guarding an already-trapped animal on שבת and שמואל's three cases of פטור ומותר; the new perek on trapping and wounding the שמונה שרצים and whether they have skin.
overview: The גמרא opens with רב's ruling: if a bird flew under a person's clothing on שבת, he may sit and guard it until nightfall. It tests this against the משנה of the second person sitting in a doorway where a deer is already trapped. The comparison to locking one's own house proves that he is פטור ומותר (fully permitted), so the משנה supports רב. This is told in two versions: as a challenge that gets answered, and as a proof that survives pushback. שמואל then teaches that every פטור on שבת means פטור אבל אסור, except three cases: the deer, draining an abscess, and trapping a snake so it won't bite. He gives a source for each. The chapter האורג ends, and a new משנה rules on trapping and wounding the שמונה שרצים, other creeping creatures, and animals already in one's possession. The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the שמונה שרצים have skin. שמואל says רבי יוחנן בן נורי, while רב says even the רבנן agree regarding שבת. A ברייתא then challenges רב, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב: You may guard a bird that flew under your clothing
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a bird entered under a person's garment on שבת, he may sit and guard it until dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אבא said in the name of רב חייא בר אשי, who said in the name of רב: If a bird went in under a person's clothing flaps, he may sit and keep it there until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling of רב: a person may sit still and keep a bird trapped under his clothes on שבת until nightfall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird is already trapped, and the person did nothing to trap it. He is only keeping it from escaping. רב says that this is allowed even לכתחילה (from the start), which is why the next steps examine whether that fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Bird
The flaps or corners of his garment
Guards it; keeps it from escaping
Until it gets dark (the end of שבת)

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
If a bird entered under the flaps of his garment —
he may sit and guard it until it gets dark.
phrases.notes: Implies he may do this לכתחילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה about trapping a deer by sitting in the doorway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may sit and guard an already-trapped bird under his clothes until nightfall; this is permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: Objection from the משנה of the second person in the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק cites the משנה where the second sitter is פטור. He suggests this means פטור אבל אסור, which would contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: The first person sat in the doorway and filled it. A second person came and sat beside him. Even if the first one got up and left, the first is liable and the second is exempt. Doesn't 'exempt' mean exempt but still forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב using the משנה about the deer trapped by a person sitting in the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the second person is only keeping in a deer that was already trapped, just like the bird in רב's case. Usually 'פטור' on שבת means no Torah punishment but still rabbinically forbidden. If that is the meaning here, then guarding an already-trapped animal is forbidden, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
The doorway
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden (rabbinically)
Is it not so that...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objected:
If the first person sat in the doorway and filled it,
phrases.notes: This traps the deer inside, which counts as צידה.

phrases.english: and the second came and sat beside him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָמַד הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָלַךְ לוֹ —
phrases.english: even if the first got up and went away —
the first is liable and the second is exempt.
Does this not mean exempt, but forbidden?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may guard an already-trapped bird לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second sitter in the משנה is in the same position as the bird-guarder. If 'פטור' there means אסור, then רב's permission contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: No: the mishnah means exempt and permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'פטור' here means פטור ומותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means exempt and permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the משנה's 'exempt' as fully permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on assuming the usual meaning of פטור. The answer says that in this case פטור means there is no prohibition at all. So the משנה actually matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt and permitted; no prohibition at all

phrases.english: No, exempt and permitted.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the term פטור in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פטור in the משנה means פטור אבל אסור, contradicting רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here פטור means פטור ומותר, so the משנה agrees with רב.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's comparison to locking one's house
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה compares the second sitter to someone who locks his house and finds a deer trapped inside. That is clearly permitted, so the second sitter is פטור ומותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, since the end of the משנה teaches: What is this like? Like someone who locks his house to protect it and a deer turns out to be guarded inside. This shows that he is exempt and permitted. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the last line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking your own house on שבת is obviously allowed, even if an animal happens to be inside. Since the משנה compares the second sitter to that, his action must also be fully permitted. 'שמע מינה' confirms the point.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical (introduces supporting evidence)
The latter clause of a משנה
To what is this similar?
By inference; this implies
Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: The second person in the doorway is פטור ומותר, just like someone who locks his house with a deer inside. So רב is right that one may guard an already-trapped bird.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since the latter clause teaches:
To what is this similar? —
To one who locks his house to guard it
and a deer turns out to be guarded inside it,
which implies that he is exempt and permitted!
Learn from it.

steps.raayaObject: The reading that the second sitter is פטור ומותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה comparing the case to locking one's house with a deer inside.

steps.title: Second version: the משנה supports רב
steps.stepSummary: In an alternate version, רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the same משנה as support for רב: the second sitter is פטור ומותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We too learned this. Even if the first got up and left, the first is liable and the second exempt. Doesn't that mean exempt and permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רב נחמן בר יצחק's words. Here he uses the משנה as a proof for רב, not as an objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts and the משנה stay the same; only the direction of the argument flips. In this version רב נחמן assumes פטור means פטור ומותר and offers it as support. The next step tests that assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (introduces an alternate version)
We too have learned it (introduces support)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same discussion told the other way around: here the משנה is a proof for רב rather than a challenge against him.

phrases.english: Some say,
Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
We too have learned it:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָמַד הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָלַךְ לוֹ —
phrases.english: Even if the first got up and went away —
the first is liable and the second exempt,
does this not mean exempt and permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 2–4 in an alternate version, as support instead of challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that guarding an already-trapped bird is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the second sitter is פטור.

steps.title: Pushback: maybe it means exempt but forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof by suggesting פטור here means פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means exempt but forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by offering the usual reading of פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פטור here carries its normal שבת meaning, the משנה gives no support to רב. It would even suggest guarding the bird is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: No (introduces a rejection)

phrases.english: No, exempt but forbidden.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the משנה as support for רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes פטור means מותר, but usually on שבת פטור means אסור.

steps.title: The house-locking comparison defeats the pushback
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the סיפא's comparison to locking one's house proves the case is פטור ומותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה teaches: What is this like? Like one who locks his house to guard it and a deer is found guarded inside. This implies exempt and permitted. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The pushback is refuted using the same סיפא of the משנה, and the support for רב stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking your own house is clearly allowed. Comparing the second sitter to that shows his action is also fully permitted, so the proof for רב holds.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (introduces a counterpoint)
Locks
Deer

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way: the משנה's comparison to locking a house proves פטור ומותר, which supports רב.

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:
To what is this similar? —
To one who locks his house to guard it,
and a deer turns out to be guarded inside it,
which implies exempt and permitted.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the דחיה of step 6 and confirms the proof of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the second sitter is פטור ומותר, supporting רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא's comparison to locking one's house with a deer inside.

steps.title: שמואל: every exemption on שבת is forbidden, except three
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that all פטורים on שבת mean פטור אבל אסור, except three cases that are פטור ומותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: All the 'exempt' rulings of שבת mean exempt but forbidden, except these three, which are exempt and permitted:
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל states a general rule about the word פטור on שבת. He is setting up a list of three exceptions, which the next steps present one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the deer case needed proof: by default פטור means אסור. Only three cases break that pattern, and שמואל will give a source for each.

keyTerms.meaning: The exemptions in the laws of שבת
Except for these three

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key general rule for all of מסכת שבת: unless you are dealing with one of these three cases, 'פטור' means the act is still forbidden rabbinically.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
All exemptions of Shabbat
are exempt but forbidden,
except for these three
which are exempt and permitted:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands from the deer case to a general rule about פטור on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every פטור on שבת is פטור אבל אסור, except three cases that are פטור ומותר.

steps.title: First exception: the deer, with its source
steps.stepSummary: The first exception is the deer case. Its source is the משנה's comparison to locking one's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is this case. And how do we know it is exempt and permitted? Because the end of the משנה teaches: What is this like? Like one who locks his house to guard it and a deer is found guarded inside.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל names the first exception, the deer case just discussed, and the גמרא proves it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the same one the גמרא already used: the comparison to locking one's own house shows the act is fully allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: One (the first item)
And from where do we know?

phrases.english: One is this,
and from where do we know it is exempt and permitted? —
Because the latter clause teaches:
To what is this similar? —
To one who locks his house to guard it,
and a deer turns out to be guarded inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First item in שמואל's list from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the deer case is פטור ומותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה (locking one's house).

steps.title: Second exception: draining an abscess
steps.stepSummary: Opening an abscess (מורסא) to make a lasting opening is חייב. Opening it only to let out fluid is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another: One who punctures an abscess on שבת — if to make it an opening, he is liable; if to let out fluid from it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל presents the second exception: draining an abscess just to release the pus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a lasting opening counts as a creative act, so it is חייב. Just letting fluid out is פטור, and the next step shows it is even permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the next item)
One who punctures or drains
An abscess or boil filled with pus
Fluid (pus)

phrases.english: And another:
One who punctures an abscess on Shabbat,
if to make an opening for it — he is liable,
if to let out fluid from it — he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Draining an abscess only to release fluid is פטור (and, as shown next, permitted).

steps.title: Source: a hand needle may be used to remove a thorn
steps.stepSummary: A משנה allows moving a sewing needle on שבת to take out a thorn. So piercing the skin to release something is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know it is exempt and permitted? As we learned: A hand needle — may be used to remove a thorn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that draining the abscess is fully permitted, using a משנה about removing a thorn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a thorn is like draining an abscess: you open the skin only to take something out. Since the משנה even allows moving a needle for that purpose, the act must be מותר, not just פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A hand (sewing) needle
Thorn or splinter

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is exempt and permitted?
As we learned:
A hand needle —
may be used to remove a thorn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּפָטוּר וּמוּתָּר? דִּתְנַן: מַחַט שֶׁל יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the second exception.
steps.raayaObject: That draining an abscess for its fluid is פטור ומותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting a hand needle to remove a thorn.

steps.title: Third exception: trapping a snake to avoid its bite
steps.stepSummary: Catching a snake to keep it from biting is פטור. Catching it for medicine is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another: One who traps a snake on שבת — if he deals with it so it won't bite him, he is exempt; if for medicine, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל presents the third exception: catching a snake only to protect oneself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trapping for a use, like medicine, is real צידה and is חייב. Trapping only to stop it from biting is פטור, and the next step shows it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: One who traps
Snake
Deals or busies himself with it
Medicine, healing

phrases.english: And another:
One who traps a snake on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִתְעַסֵּק בּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְּׁכֶנּוּ — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if he deals with it so it won't bite him — he is exempt,
if for medicine — he is liable,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping a snake only to avoid being bitten is פטור (and, as shown next, permitted).

steps.title: Source: covering a lamp, feces, or a scorpion with a bowl
steps.stepSummary: A משנה permits overturning a bowl over a lamp, a child's feces, or a scorpion. This shows protective acts like covering a dangerous creature are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know it is exempt and permitted? As we learned: One may overturn a bowl over a lamp so it won't catch the ceiling beam, and over a child's feces, and over a scorpion so it won't bite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that trapping a snake to prevent a bite is permitted, from a משנה about covering a scorpion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering a scorpion with a bowl traps it, yet the משנה allows it לכתחילה to prevent a bite. The same applies to a snake, so that case is פטור ומותר.

keyTerms.meaning: One may overturn a bowl
Ceiling beam
Scorpion

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's three cases that are פטור ומותר: (1) guarding an already-trapped deer, (2) draining an abscess for its fluid, (3) trapping a snake so it won't bite. Every other פטור on שבת is אסור.

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is exempt and permitted? —
As we learned:
One may overturn a bowl over a lamp
so that it won't catch the ceiling beam,
and over a child's feces,
and over a scorpion so it won't bite.
phrases.notes: This is the part that proves the snake case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּפָטוּר וּמוּתָּר? דִּתְנַן: כּוֹפִין קְעָרָה עַל הַנֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the third exception.
steps.raayaObject: That trapping a snake to avoid its bite is פטור ומותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting overturning a bowl over a scorpion so it won't bite.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter of האורג
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק האורג.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter האורג.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter האורג ends here with the traditional closing formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הדרן עלך' expresses the learner's commitment to return to this chapter. It is not part of the legal argument.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (formula ending a chapter)
The Weaver — the name of this chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaOreg

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after שמואל's list.

steps.title: The משנה: trapping and wounding different creatures
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets three rules. For the שמונה שרצים, both trapping and wounding make you חייב. For other creeping creatures, wounding is פטור, and trapping is חייב only if done for a need. For animals and birds you already own, trapping is פטור but wounding is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The eight creeping animals mentioned in the תורה: one who traps them or wounds them is liable. Other repulsive and crawling creatures: one who wounds them is exempt. One who traps them for a need is liable, and one who traps them not for a need is exempt. An animal or bird that is already in his possession: one who traps it is exempt, and one who wounds it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new perek begins with a משנה. It sorts creatures into three groups and says when trapping or wounding them on שבת makes a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wounding (חובל) only counts when there is a real wound, meaning blood gathers under the skin. That is why it matters whether a creature has proper skin. Trapping (צידה) only counts when the creature is not already caught, so an animal you already own cannot be trapped, but it can still be wounded.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight creeping animals listed in ויקרא י״א (like the mole, mouse, and lizard)
One who traps; צידה is one of the ל״ט מלאכות
One who wounds, causing a real wound where blood gathers under the skin
Other repulsive and crawling creatures
For a need, meaning the trapping serves a real purpose
In his possession, meaning already caught

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two מלאכות. An animal you own can still be wounded on שבת even though it can no longer be trapped. Trapping and wounding are judged separately.

phrases.english: MISHNA
The eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah
one who traps them or wounds them is liable
and other repulsive and crawling creatures:
one who wounds them is exempt
phrases.notes: Wounding them does not count as a real wound.

phrases.english: one who traps them for a need is liable
not for a need, he is exempt
An animal or bird that is in his possession:
one who traps it is exempt
and one who wounds it is liable

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek right after the הדרן of פרק האורג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמונה שרצים: trapping and wounding are חייב. Other creatures: wounding is פטור, and trapping is חייב only לצורך. Animals in one's possession: trapping is פטור, wounding is חייב.

steps.title: The משנה assumes the eight creatures have skin. Whose view is that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from "הַחוֹבֵל בָּהֶן חַיָּיב" that the שמונה שרצים have real skin. It then asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since the משנה teaches "one who wounds them is liable," we can infer that they have skin. Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה's wording. It then asks whose opinion that inference matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You are only חייב for wounding when there is skin that holds the blood in. So by making wounding חייב, the משנה shows it holds that these creatures have true skin. Since that point is disputed elsewhere, the גמרא wants to know which side the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the discussion of the משנה
By inference, it follows that
Skin
Who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this)

phrases.english: GEMARA
From the fact that it teaches "one who wounds them is liable"
we can infer that they have skin
Who is the Tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי הַחוֹבֵל בָּהֶן חַיָּיב מִכְּלָל דְּאִית לְהוּ עוֹר מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה's first clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the שמונה שרצים have skin.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. In another משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the eight שרצים have skins.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: This is the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. As we learned in a משנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: The eight creeping animals have skins.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by naming the תנא. He backs this up with another משנה where רבי יוחנן בן נורי says all eight שרצים have skins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That other משנה is about טומאה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that the skin of all eight is separate from the flesh, while the רבנן treat the skin of some of them like flesh. שמואל assumes that whoever says "they have skin" there would also say it here for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Skins
A תנא who holds that all eight שרצים have true skins

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as we learned: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
The eight creeping animals have skins

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that all eight שרצים have skins.

steps.title: רב: even the רבנן agree regarding שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה can even match the רבנן. Their argument with רבי יוחנן בן נורי is only about טומאה, based on the פסוק "אֵלֶּה הַטְּמֵאִים לָכֶם". For שבת, they agree that these creatures have skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: You can even say it is the רבנן. The רבנן only argue with רבי יוחנן בן נורי about טומאה, as it says "These are impure for you," which comes to include that their skins are like their flesh. But for שבת, even the רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב offers a different answer from שמואל's. He says the משנה does not have to follow only רבי יוחנן בן נורי, because the רבנן would agree on this point as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן treat the skin like flesh only because a special פסוק says so for טומאה. That פסוק does not change the physical fact that the creature has skin. So for wounding on שבת, everyone agrees the skin is real skin, and wounding is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן
They only argue up to this point (and no further)
Ritual impurity
To include (a derivation from a פסוק)
They agree

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן do not deny that these creatures have skin. They only say that for טומאה the פסוק treats the skin like flesh. That is a special rule for טומאה, not a statement that there is no skin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a dispute in one area of הלכה (טומאה) may not carry over to another area (שבת), because the reason for the dispute is specific to the first area.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:
You can even say it is the Rabbis
The Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
regarding impurity
as it is written: "These are the impure for you"
to include that their skins are like their flesh
But regarding Shabbat
even the Rabbis agree

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the מאן תנא question, widening שמואל's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow everyone, because the רבנן's view that skin is like flesh applies only to טומאה, derived from a פסוק.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא shows they do argue about Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב. A ברייתא says that wounding one of the eight שרצים is חייב according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and then begins to quote the חכמים disagreeing. The text continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding שבת they do not disagree?! But it was taught in a ברייתא: One who traps one of the eight creeping animals mentioned in the תורה, or one who wounds them, is liable. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. And the חכמים say: Skin is only...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's claim that the רבנן agree about שבת. It brings a ברייתא where the חכמים seem to argue about wounding these creatures on שבת. The quote breaks off mid-sentence and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is explicitly about שבת (trapping and wounding). Since it records a dispute between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the חכמים, it looks like they do argue about שבת, which contradicts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
The words of (marks whose opinion it is)
And the חכמים say (the opposing view)

phrases.english: And regarding Shabbat they do not disagree?!
But it was taught in a baraita:
One who traps one of the eight creeping animals
mentioned in the Torah
or one who wounds them is liable
These are the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
And the Sages say:
Skin is only...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the רבנן agree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי regarding שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about trapping and wounding on שבת records the חכמים disagreeing with רבי יוחנן בן נורי. That suggests a dispute about שבת as well.
